text:
marta: Noticed surge alerts on eu2: dedicated-pool-beta. Many requests spilled to shared and cross-az egress shot up. Tail latency 3-4x and tenant reports inconsistent model variants.
leo: Do we have a topology change or reimage window?
marta: No planned maintenance. alloc-bot: Host pm-88 reimaged at 6611111500 (auto-reimage), auto-ssh:failed -> recovered.
rachel: Reimage often clears carveout markers, but if fence GC doesn't run we get stale ownership. Can you run `allocctl dump --host pm-88 --format=short`?
marta: pasted: `HOST:pm-88 markers:[{slice:dedicated-pool-b, owner:dedicated-pool-b, hb:6611109000},{slice:dedicated-pool-c, owner:dedicated-pool-c, hb:6611108000}]` but alloc logs show pm-88 serving pool-b and pool-c concurrently for a short window.
leo: That marker list looks ok, but why cross-az egress spiked? Check router decisions: `router-eu2` sent ~200 requests to route=rack-fallback-usw because local slice reported ALLOC_OK but network path had high RTT, router misrouted to shared path.
tyler: Could be that after reimage host attached to a different TOR with a stale BGP next-hop, causing transient cross-az egress. Net team had a BGP flap earlier at 6611111400.
rachel: So two issues intersecting: stale carveout markers + network path change => requests routed off-host and hit cold shared caches => noisy neighbor-like behavior.
alloc-bot: Recent interlock events: 5 interlock_conflict entries in last 15m across pm-70..pm-95.
marta: Immediate asks: 1) run carveout-GC on pm-88 and pm-92, 2) add router soft-hold when interlock_conflict detected for dedicated slices (hold 1s before fallback), 3) throttle cross-az fallback rate so we don't flood shared caches.
leo: For (2) soft-hold: router already has quick-fallback window at 250ms. Propose we gate dedicated-slice fallbacks behind a 1s soft-hold and emit metric `router.dedicated.soft_hold_hits`.
tyler: For (3) add a rate cap: `router.fallback.cross_az_rate_limit=30rps` per cluster. That keeps cache pollution bounded.
rachel: I'm worried about pager noise. Add alert dedupe: if interlock_conflict > 3 hosts in 5m, escalate; else just fire perf alert.
ci-bot: Started job: job_id=gc-6611113300 run_by=marta on hosts=[pm-88,pm-92].
marta: GC job completed, markers refreshed; allocctl now shows `hb:6611115800` for affected slices.
leo: Re-ran health checks: router still sending a few fallbacks but most traffic back to dedicated models, latency dropping.
tyler: Network team confirmed TOR flap and applied ?fix at 6611113600. Cross-az egress normalized.
rachel: Lessons: 1) prefill/lease expiry needs stronger guarantees; boolean marker too brittle when network/topology churn happens. 2) router should be conservative about degrading dedicated tenants. 3) add cross-az egress cost accounting to show impact.
leo: Cost ask: can someone estimate token-cost delta? I suspect cross-az + fallback cold-cache multiplies cost by 2.5x for affected requests.
marta: Quick calc: ~320k tokens affected, baseline cost $0.08/1k tokens => baseline $25.6. With 2.5x => extra $38.4 => delta ~$38 (not trivial).
rachel: Ouch. We'll include that in the postmortem. For longer term: implement lease token with TTL and renew-on-heartbeat + reconciler to sweep markers if host identity changes. Also add a `router.defer_on_interlock` flag default true.
leo: I'll file an RFC for carveout-lease model and router defer semantics. Can we spin up an experiment to enable `router.defer_on_interlock` in eu2 for 24h?
marta: Yes, turn it on for eu2 canary now. tyler: I want a rollback plan: if we see 5% higher 95p latency for shared customers, flip off.
alloc-bot: Experiment flag toggled: router.defer_on_interlock=enabled for eu2 (canary).
ci-bot: Incident created: /incidents/6611112222-eu2-reimage-marker-network-fallout assigned to eng-infra + networking.
leo: Thanks team. Keep monitoring router.dedicated.soft_hold_hits and interlock_conflict counts. Update this thread with any regression. :thumbsup:
